profile.headline: Engineer, educator, and researcher working where business, engineering, and AI meet
profile.bio: I spent years as a high-tech engineer in advanced manufacturing before moving into business education. Today I teach business analytics and research methods, lead student capstone projects, and research how AI is reshaping business and engineering practice. I believe the hardest and most interesting problems now sit between disciplines.
profile.bio2: This site is my working window into three areas: student experiential learning projects built on real business problems; AI Watch, a curated list of impactful AI videos, articles, and papers; and Diamond Market Watch, a biweekly tracker of natural and lab-grown diamond prices.
profile.statement: Built on real-world data and live business scenarios, these student projects train the judgment textbooks can’t, and several led to public presentations and showcases.

projects.title: Bringing Solar Light to the North San Joaquin Valley

numbers.intro: In one year, the team moved from an idea to evidence: a formal industry partnership, field-tested products, AI-assisted market research across the region, and direct engagement with campus leaders, businesses, investors, and the community.

student learning.name: Student learning
items: Students owned research, data analysis, and reporting on a biweekly cycle, and 2 of the 3 research assistants were hired by the time the project ended.
Biweekly reviews with Portor Lighting and a visit to its facility in Ontario, CA put students alongside industry veterans in product, manufacturing, and sales.

AI was part of the workflow, not a side topic. The team used AI tools such as Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, HeyGen, and Newport AI to build domain knowledge, brainstorm ideas, prepare and analyze data, write code, generate leads, craft stories for different audiences, and produce outreach videos with digital avatars.
Students presented at school events, joined an investor pitch, and met with campus leaders, local businesses, and regional organizations, using AI to shape the storytelling and outreach materials.
Students developed a technician training framework, a bill of materials, and a U.S. supplier list that prepare the project for its next phase.
student learning.intro: The project was designed as experiential learning. Students did the work of a startup team, with real stakes, real partners, and real deadlines.

subs.title: Field test of the solar bollard
subs.text: Pilot installations at residential sites in Northern California and on-campus demonstrations tested how the solar bollard performs at night, including its battery and electrical output.

subs.title: LightScope campus siting map
subs.text: A night-time field survey of University of the Pacific sites became an interactive siting map: 13 lighting zones, 28 assessed points, and 64 planned fixture locations.

subs.title: AI lead-intelligence platform
subs.text: AI agents drew on six public data sources to find and rank places that could benefit from solar lighting: 300+ potential sites identified and 100+ opportunities ranked across 13 market segments.

subs.title: Live market dashboard
subs.text: With AI-assisted data preparation and coding, students built an e-commerce and residential dashboard in SQL, Python, and Google Looker Studio, combining market research and competitor analysis to support decisions.

subs.title: Bill of materials and U.S. suppliers
subs.text: Students built a bill of materials (BOM) for a commercial solar bollard and identified U.S. vendors for its components, paving the way for domestic, BABA-compliant manufacturing in the next stage.

subs.title: Market, supplier, and IP landscape
subs.text: AI tools helped the team build domain knowledge quickly. The result was a competitive analysis of the solar lighting market, supported by legal consulting to understand the intellectual property landscape of the U.S. solar lighting industry.

subs.title: Pitch, video, and community outreach
subs.text: An investor pitch at Smart Living Silicon Valley 2026, a pilot proposal for Stockton's Miracle Mile, and an "Invest in Stockton" outreach video on clean-energy manufacturing, presented by an AI digital avatar.

subs.title: Workforce training framework
subs.text: A training framework for Solar Light Product Assembly Technicians, with a plan to grow it into a high school summer camp, plus an AI-assisted marketing lecture for local workforce development.

emerging needs and opportunities.name: Emerging needs and opportunities
items: Interest in safe, sustainable lighting is growing across campuses, communities, and public spaces in the region.
Organizations want proven, low-risk solutions before they invest.
Domestic clean-energy manufacturing and skilled local jobs remain regional priorities.
We welcome conversations with institutions, companies, and investors interested in collaborating on the next phase.

long-term vision.name: Long-term vision
items: A new local entity, a pilot manufacturing facility, and a BABA-compliant prototype
Manufacturing, sales, and service operations reach break-even
A fully operational manufacturer with protected IP and in-house design, manufacturing, and installation
long-term vision.intro: With Phase II grant funding or venture investment, the project could grow in three steps:

student voices.name: Student voices
items: This was my chance to actually do the work: research, build a dashboard, and eventually sit across the table from executives and project managers, making the case for why this matters and how it can change sustainability in our community.

The project gave me a real environment where effort had consequences. I had to learn AI, build systems, assess sites at night, organize data, prepare proposals, speak with professionals, manage relationships, and continue even when the main result, a closed sale, had not happened yet.

One of the most valuable parts of this experience was working on a project with multiple stakeholders and open-ended engineering challenges. Unlike many classroom assignments, this project required collaboration, organization, and problem-solving throughout the entire process.

outcomes.name: Outcomes
items: The project grew well beyond its original scope. Students left with professional experience that led directly to jobs, the industry partner expressed interest in hosting more student interns, and the work produced reusable tools and new community connections that will support future projects in the region.

We are also grateful to University of the Pacific Sustainability, Facilities, Engineering, and Public Safety, and to the community partners who shared their time and insight.

projects.status: Completed · ready for the next phase
projects.summary: Funded by North Valley Thrive, this one-year project assessed the viability of bringing solar lighting products, and ultimately clean-energy manufacturing, to the North San Joaquin Valley. Working with industry partner Portor Lighting, a faculty-led team of three student research assistants confirmed market and community interest and identified lighting needs across campuses, residential communities, and public spaces. The team also used AI to build market intelligence, studied the U.S. supply chain and the intellectual property landscape, confirmed a pathway to Buy America (BABA 2021) compliance, and developed a training framework for local technicians. The project is now ready for its next stage.
